name: Silkpeel
lead: SilkPeel is a branded diamond-tip dermabrasion treatment, a gentle exfoliating facial performed in a clinic or medspa. It is used to smooth rough texture, brighten dull skin, and soften fine lines and mild sun damage, so skin looks fresher and more even.[1]

Diamond-tip systems use a roughened wand with fine diamond particles bonded to the surface instead of the aluminum oxide crystals of older microdermabrasion machines. Because no crystals are blown into the air, they are considered easier to use near the eyes and lips, and diamond tips date to 1999.[1] Treatments are typically repeated every few weeks, since results from this lighter class of exfoliation are temporary.[1]

chain: Diamond-tip wand removes the outer dead skin layer
Skin looks brighter and more even
angle.text: A diamond-tip wand polishes away the outermost layer of dead skin, leaving a smoother, brighter surface. People book series of sessions for texture, dullness and mild pigmentation.

paras: Microdermabrasion is a non-surgical exfoliation that removes only the outermost dead layer of skin, usually with an abrasive and suction. It is used for superficial hyperpigmentation, sun damage, fine lines, mild acne and shallow scars, and can help skincare products absorb better.[1] SilkPeel is a commercial diamond-tip form of this approach, and the name is also used by providers for the same style of facial.

The first microdermabrasion unit was developed in Italy in 1985 with aluminum oxide crystals; the FDA approved the first machines in 1996 and they reached the US market in 1997. Diamond tips followed in 1999, bristle tips in 2005 and crystal-free vacuum systems in 2012.[1]

Microdermabrasion has few side effects, mostly temporary dryness and sun sensitivity, with occasional bruising or scratches. Crystal-based systems carry a risk of eye injury and inhalation, which diamond-tip systems avoid.[1] Deeper dermabrasion, a separate surgical procedure, involves bleeding and healing over roughly 7 to 30 days.[1]

timeline.event: First microdermabrasion unit developed in Italy.[1]

card.summary: A diamond-tip exfoliating facial that polishes away dull outer skin for a smoother, brighter complexion.
card.note: Results are temporary; sessions are repeated.

quick.overview:
SilkPeel is a diamond-tip dermabrasion facial. A provider glides a fine diamond-surfaced wand over the skin to remove the top layer of dead cells.

People use it to improve texture, dullness, fine lines and mild pigmentation, usually as a series of sessions.
quick.mechanism: The abrasive tip, often paired with suction, gently removes the outermost skin layer, revealing smoother skin and helping products penetrate better.
quick.risks: Side effects are usually mild and temporary: dryness, sun sensitivity, occasional bruising. Results fade, so sessions are repeated every few weeks.
